title: B2B ABM Go-Live: Relationship-Grain Activation Under a Deadline

moves.dialogueText: "ABM goes live in two weeks, and buying committees put one Contact on several Accounts. Mapping a real Account Contact relationship costs a day of harmonization we do not have. Can we map Account Contact straight from Contact and keep moving?"

options.text: Map Account Contact from the Account–Contact relationship object, related to both Account and Individual.
options.techDebtImpact: Costs a day of harmonization now, but each Contact–Account pair gets its own row, which later activations can use as their membership grain.

options.text: Map Account Contact one-to-one from Contact so modeling finishes today and activation planning starts tomorrow.
options.techDebtImpact: Saves a day now, but one row per Contact cannot represent a Contact on several Accounts, so later activations lose which Account each row belongs to.

moves.dialogueText: "The junction DMO is still in the Other category. Moving it to Profile means recreating or transforming it and re-testing its relationships, about half a sprint. Can we leave it as Other and still use it for Activation Membership?"

options.text: Leave the junction in the Other category and rely on its Account and Contact relationships to make it selectable.
options.techDebtImpact: Saves half a sprint now, but only Profile-category DMOs can define activation members, so marketing falls back to Contact membership.

options.text: Recreate the junction in the Profile category, re-relate it to Account and Contact, and select it for membership.
options.techDebtImpact: Costs half a sprint now, but Profile is the category Activation Membership requires, so the junction becomes selectable.

moves.dialogueText: "In the dry run, a Contact on two Accounts came out as one Data Extension row, and the second Account's attributes were missing. Re-segmenting on the junction and changing membership takes another build day. Leadership says keep Contact membership and let Marketing Cloud sort it out. Do we?"

options.text: Keep Contact as the membership object and look up each Contact's Accounts inside Marketing Cloud journeys.
options.techDebtImpact: Saves a build day now, but Contact membership outputs one row per Contact, so every journey must rebuild the Account context the activation dropped.

options.text: Segment on the junction rows, set the junction as Activation Membership, and pull Contact attributes through relationships.
options.techDebtImpact: Costs a build day now, but membership on the junction outputs one row per Account–Contact pair, each carrying its own Account attributes.

moves.dialogueText: "Compliance wants every Contact Point Email in the Data Extension, but Max # of Attribute Values is locked at 1. A fan-out transform plus a new segment and activation is a multi-day track. Can we raise the attribute limit instead?"

options.text: Build a transform that outputs one row per Individual and email, then segment and activate on it.
options.techDebtImpact: Costs several days of transform and activation work, but each email becomes its own Data Extension row that Marketing Cloud can address.

options.text: Raise Max # of Attribute Values on a custom activation DMO and keep the current membership object.
options.techDebtImpact: Saves several days now, but a higher limit packs the extra emails onto the same Individual row, which Marketing Cloud cannot send to.

moves.dialogueText: "Activation fails because three attributes named Id collide across Individual, Contact Point Email, and the Redshift DMO. I can give them preferred activation names this afternoon, or we rebuild the Redshift DMO with non-overlapping field names first—three days, past go-live. Which do we do?"

options.text: Assign preferred activation names to the three colliding Id attributes and re-run the activation today.
options.techDebtImpact: Saves three days now at no later cost: the collision lives in the activation payload, so distinct names fix the Data Extension columns without touching the model.

options.text: Rebuild the Redshift DMO with non-overlapping field names, then re-run the activation after go-live.
options.techDebtImpact: Buys a tidier source model, but spends three days past go-live on a collision that payload names already resolve.
